finding.claim: A malicious SCP server can send an E record before any D record in Download(string, DirectoryInfo), driving directoryCounter negative and walking currentDirectoryFullName up to ancestor directories, so subsequent C records write attacker-chosen files there via FileMode.Create.
finding.source: Server-sent SCP protocol records read by ReadString at ScpClient.cs:895 (attacker-controlled peer).
finding.sink: new FileInfo(Path.Combine(currentDirectoryFullName, fileName)) and fileInfo.Open(FileMode.Create, FileAccess.Write) at ScpClient.cs:963-966.

trace.note: Download(string, DirectoryInfo) sends 'scp -prf' and calls InternalDownload with the DirectoryInfo.
directoryCounter initialised to 0; no check that a D record precedes E/C records.
break only when counter == 0, so not taken at -1.
currentDirectoryFullName set to parent of destination directory.
Path.Combine places file in parent directory.
FileMode.Create truncates/overwrites target file; content from server.
counter != 0 so loop continues; further E records walk higher up the tree.

finding.guards_checked: EnsureValidLocalName (ScpClient.cs:840-853) rejects empty, '.', '..', and invalid filename chars but does not bound directory depth. Break condition at 903 only fires at exactly 0. No check that E matches a prior D; no check counter >= 0. Debug.Assert at 910 is a no-op in release builds; root case gives NRE (crash, not escape). Expertise decoy 26 (canonical-prefix confinement) does not apply: no containment check exists.

finding.claim: Host key trust fails open: CanTrustHostKey returns true when no HostKeyReceived handler is attached, and HostKeyEventArgs defaults CanTrust to true, so any host key is accepted unless the caller explicitly rejects it.
finding.source: Server-presented host key and signature during key exchange, from a network-position (MITM) attacker.
finding.sink: Trust decision in ValidateExchangeHash: keyAlgorithm.VerifySignature(...) && CanTrustHostKey(keyAlgorithm) at KeyExchange.cs:493.

trace.note: Signature verified against presented key, then CanTrustHostKey consulted.
handlers = HostKeyReceived; if null, returns true at line 478.
Constructor sets CanTrust = true by default.
BaseClient always subscribes Session_HostKeyReceived to session.HostKeyReceived.
Session_HostKeyReceived forwards to public HostKeyReceived event, which defaults to trusting.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification (KeyExchange.cs:493) only proves possession of the presented key, not identity; no key pinning or known-hosts check in the library. Trust is solely dependent on caller setting CanTrust=false in a HostKeyReceived handler. Likely intentional API design; flagged because it weakens server authentication by default.
